  Findings

  HIGH     F1   sshd is open to any source on 22/tcp                                              -5
                IPv4: accepted by filter/IN_public_allow rule #1.
                filter/IN_public_allow #1:  -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,UNTRACKED -j ACCEPT
                  reached by INPUT #5 → INPUT_ZONES #1 → IN_public #3
                fix  firewalld manages this rule, and a change made with iptables is lost when it
                     writes its rules again. If the clients are known, allow the port for them and
                     remove it for all others.
                     Allow the known clients:
                       firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="<trusted-cidr>" port port="22" protocol="tcp" accept'
                     Remove the port for any source (when the zone lists it as a service, use
                     --remove-service=NAME):
                       firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-port=22/tcp
                     Load the permanent configuration:
                       firewall-cmd --reload
